messages:
Maria: deploy-bot just flagged a publish anomaly for my-service:2026-03-20 (build bld-8943). layer-index interleave caused manifest push to skip. canary saw digest sha256:old instead of new. @Devon @Jake can you triage?

deploy-bot: [automated] publish check failed: layer index interleave detected; manifest push aborted. repo=redwood/my-service, region=us-east-1, build=bld-8943

Devon: looking now. rough idea from logs? canary traffic degraded? :thinking_face:

Maria: canary errors = elevated 5xx for image pull verification, not app errors. seems image manifest on mirror got older layer order, clients prefer digest -> mismatch.

Jake: ok prob is push ordering to ECR mirror. CI pushed layers concurrently, index list returned in different order on mirror nodes -> cosign/provenance check sees mismatch. low risk for rollout but canary failing image verification.

Devon: options: 1) force-republish same build with serialized layer upload to ensure ordering; 2) pin canary to previous stable digest and rollback; 3) quick manual promote of previous digest to canary.

Maria: we need decision fast. release window in 30m. if we hold, we should pin and abort rollout.

release-manager: I'd prefer hold and pin. customers in current canary are internal only, but we want to avoid production drift. recommend hold release and update release notes with hold reason.

Jake: agreed. I'll try republish to staging with serialized upload. command I will run:```bash
deploybot republish --repo redwood/my-service --build bld-8943 --serialize-layers --target staging
```

Devon: add `--skip-canary-auto-promote` and also run a quick manifest-verify:```bash
oci-manifest-verify --repo redwood/my-service --digest sha256:new --region us-east-1
```

sre_bot: FYI created incident INC-2026-0310-1 (low) to track the mirror ordering issue and notify registry team.

Maria: Jake, once staging republish succeeds, please run a canary pull verification and post the output. If green, we can decide to re-run rollout. If not, we'll pin to previous digest and cancel release.

Jake: started republish now. logs:```
[2026-03-20T15:07:12Z] upload layer 1 -> success
[2026-03-20T15:07:16Z] upload layer 2 -> success
[2026-03-20T15:07:21Z] push manifest -> success
[2026-03-20T15:07:22Z] cosign attestation -> success
[2026-03-20T15:07:25Z] mirror sync check -> ok
```

Jake: staging verify: `oci-manifest-verify` returned OK for digest sha256:new across us-east mirror set. canary pull test (from k8s node) succeeded.

Devon: running canary smoke tests now.

Devon: smoke tests pass, image verification ok. I recommend we re-run the canary promotion but with `--promote-delay 10m` so we can monitor and abort if anything pops up.

release-manager: updating release notes and change window. note: held for 18m for republish; resumed canary promote with monitoring. I'll annotate the changelog: "Hold during publish consistency check; republished serialized layers."

Maria: final decision: hold initial rollout, republished serialized layers, verified in staging, re-run canary promote with 10m delay and monitoring. if any verification fails revert to pinned digest sha256:prev and open rollback.

Jake: tagging action items: 1) I will push republish docs to infra-runbook (PR incoming). 2) Devon will add a registry test to CI for manifest ordering. 3) release-manager will add note to release notes and email #customer-updates if we had external customers in the window.

release-manager: noted and taking email action if needed. closing thread once PR + changelog done. :white_check_mark:
